The opening contains an explicit refusal to discuss a partner's abortion, followed by reproductive-health details and later display of an image. The restricted record preserves accountability while the public reader omits the material.

DC's 2013 record confirms The Sandman: Overture was written by Neil Gaiman and illustrated by J.H. Williams III, not James Jean: https://www.dc.com/blog/2013/10/30/neil-gaiman-returns-to-vertigo-with-the-sandman-overture
James Jean's own CV documents his Fables covers and Eisner recognition; the episode's superlatives remain personal praise rather than archive ranking: https://www.jamesjean.com/page-cv/
The transcript should later be reconciled against Esao Andrews and James Jean exhibition archives, David Choe's published book, Asa Akira's memoir, and surviving episode media.
summary: A crowded first episode of 2014 organized around support: whether siblings watch one another's work, whether criticism can improve craft without humiliation, whether artists need celebrity validation, and whether friendship means attendance, money, gifts or honest attention. Steve Lee's fear-induced nosebleed before a large comedy set supplies the title, but the deeper sequence is his argument with Bobby Lee over support, bombing and constructive criticism. Esao Andrews and James Jean widen the question to artistic careers, pricing, group shows, comics, fan art and the difference between acclaim and practice. The archive preserves that useful craft conversation while rejecting racial-slur permission structures, autism and suicide mockery, medical speculation, distracted driving, oil-paint hierarchy and coerced disclosure. A participant twice says private reproductive-health material should not be discussed; the public layer honors that refusal. Named dialogue remains withheld.
